1 Thessalonians, probably the oldest boo: 1 Tesalonikafo, ebia Apam Foforo nhoma a ɛyɛ dedaw sen biara: 'Mommɔ mpae a monnnyae' (1 Thessalonians 5:17).
Sts Cyril and Methodius, apostles to the: Wɔwoo Ahotefo Cyril ne Methodius, Slavfo asomafo, wɔ ha.
Where the Jews 'examined the Scriptures: Baabi a Yudafo 'hwehwɛɛ Kyerɛwnsɛm no mu da biara' sɛ wɔde bɛsɔ Paulo asɛnka ahwɛ.
The Beroeans receive the word eagerly an: Bereafo de ahopere gye asɛm no na wɔhwehwɛ Kyerɛwnsɛm no mu da biara (Acts 17:10-12).
Sopater of Beroea later travels with Pau: Akyiri yi Sopater a ofi Berea ne Paulo tu kwan (Acts 20:4).
Paul preached to the philosophers on the: Paulo ka asɛm kyerɛɛ nyansapɛfo wɔ Areopago so fa 'Onyankopɔn a wonnim no' ho.
'What you worship unknowingly, I proclai: 'Nea mosom no a munnim no no, ɛno na meka ho asɛm kyerɛ mo.' Paulo ka Onyankopɔn a 'ne mu na yɛte ase, yɛkeka yɛn ho na yɛwɔ hɔ' no ho asɛm (Acts 17:22-31).
Dionysius the Areopagite and a woman nam: Dionisio Areopagoni ne ɔbaa bi a wɔfrɛ no Damari gye di (Acts 17:34).
The Catholic Cathedral Basilica of St Di: Ɔhotefo Dionisio Areopagoni Katolek Asɔre Kɛse Basilika wɔ Atene mfinimfini.
St John Paul II visited the Areopagus in: Ɔhotefo Yohane Paulo II kɔsraa Areopago afe 2001 mu.
Busy port city where Paul worked as a te: Hyɛngyinabea kurow a nnipa dɔɔso, baabi a Paulo yɛɛ ntamadan adwuma afe ne fa; 1 ne 2 Korintofo asɔre.
Paul lives and works with Aquila and Pri: Paulo ne Akwila ne Priskila tena na wɔyɛ adwuma bom na ɔtena hɔ asram dunwɔtwe (Acts 18:1-11). Wɔde no kɔ amrado Galio anim (Acts 18:12-17).
Paul hands on what he received: 'This is: Paulo de nea ɔnyae no ma: 'Eyi ne me nipadua... Monyɛ eyi mfa nkae me', Ukaristia ho asɛm a wɔkyerɛwee a edi kan (1 Corinthians 11:23-26).
'Love is patient, love is kind' (1 Corin: 'Ɔdɔ wɔ abotare, ɔdɔ yɛ adɔe' (1 Corinthians 13). Ɔbobɔ Kristo a wasɔre no adansefo din (1 Corinthians 15:3-8).
Phoebe, a minister of the church at Cenc: Foibe, Kenkrea asɔre somfo, de Paulo krataa kɔ Roma (Romans 16:1-2).
An inscription naming Gallio fixes Paul': Nkyerɛwee bi a ɛbɔ Galio din kyerɛ sɛ Paulo tenaa Korinto bɛyɛ afe 50-52 Kristo akyi, ne nkwa mu nna a ɛyɛ pintinn sen biara no mu baako.
Around AD 96 St Clement of Rome wrote to: Bɛyɛ afe 96 Kristo akyi, Ɔhotefo Klemente a ofi Roma kyerɛw krataa kɔmaa Korintofo sɛ wonsiesie akyinnye bi, Roma asɔre no adwene a esi afoforo so ho nsɛnkyerɛnne a edi kan.
Small Aegean island where John received: Aegea supɔw ketewa a Yohane nyaa Adiyisɛm Nhoma no anisoadehu wɔ so.
'I, John, your brother... found myself o: 'Me Yohane, mo nua... na mewɔ supɔw a wɔfrɛ no Patmo so, efisɛ meka Onyankopɔn asɛm' (Revelation 1:9-11).
He sees 'a new heaven and a new earth' a: Ohu 'ɔsoro foforo ne asase foforo' ne kurow kronkron a efi Onyankopɔn nkyɛn resian aba (Revelation 21:1-4).
The Cave of the Apocalypse and the Monas: Adiyisɛm Buw ne Ɔhotefo Yohane Ahosiesifo Fie (wɔhyɛɛ ase 1088) yɛ Greek Orthodox dea ne UNESCO Wiase Agyapade Beae.
Bay on Crete's south coast where Paul's: Po kokwaa a ɛwɔ Krete anafo fam mpoano, baabi a Paulo afiase hyɛn no hintaw ansa na ahum no rebɛbɔ.
The ship reaches 'a place called Fair Ha: Hyɛn no du 'beae bi a wɔfrɛ no Hyɛngyinabea Pa' bɛn Lasea; Paulo bɔ wɔn kɔkɔ sɛ wɔnkɔ so ntu kwan (Acts 27:7-12).
Paul leaves Titus in Crete to appoint el: Paulo gyaw Tito wɔ Krete sɛ ɔnyi mpanyimfo wɔ kurow biara mu (Titus 1:5).
Capital of the empire, where Paul preach: Ahemman no ahenkurow, baabi a Paulo kaa asɛm sɛ odeduani na amammerɛ ka sɛ Petro ne Paulo de wɔn nkwa too hɔ. Petro ada da Ɔhotefo Petro Basilika ase.
Judas Maccabeus sends envoys to Rome to: Yuda Makabeo soma abɔfo kɔ Roma sɛ wɔnkɔyɛ apam (1 Maccabees 8:17-20).
Paul writes to 'all the beloved of God i: Paulo kyerɛw krataa kɔma 'Onyankopɔn adɔfo a wɔwɔ Roma nyinaa', a wɔn gyidi 'ho asɛm atrɛw wiase nyinaa' (Romans 1:7-8).
Paul arrives as a prisoner and for two y: Paulo du hɔ sɛ odeduani na mfe abien ogye wɔn a wɔba ne nkyɛn nyinaa, 'ka Onyankopɔn ahenni ho asɛm' (Acts 28:16-31).
Peter sends greetings from the church 'i: Petro kyia fi asɔre a ɛwɔ 'Babilon' no, a nnipa pii kenkan sɛ Roma (1 Peter 5:13). Yesu ka sɛnea Petro bewu ho nkɔm (John 21:18-19).
Peter was crucified on the Vatican Hill: Wɔbɔɔ Petro asɛndua mu wɔ Vatican Koko so wɔ Nero bere so, bɛyɛ afe 64-67 Kristo akyi, na Ɔhotefo Petro Basilika si ne ada so. Pius XII bɔɔ nhwehwɛmu a wɔyɛɛ wɔ afɔremuka kɛse no ase no ho dawuru afe 1950 mu.
Wotwaa Paulo ti wɔ Ostia kwan so. Ɔhotefo Paulo a Ɛwɔ Ɔfasu Akyi Basilika kora ne ada.
The Church celebrates both apostles toge: Asɔre no di asomafo baanu no nyinaa afahyɛ bom Ayɛwohomumu 29.
The busy port near Naples where Paul lan: Hyɛngyinabea a nnipa dɔɔso a ɛbɛn Naples, baabi a Paulo duu Italy na ohuu sɛ Kristofo wɔ hɔ dedaw.
At Puteoli 'we found some brothers and w: Puteoli 'yehuu anuanom bi, na wɔsrɛɛ yɛn sɛ yɛne wɔn ntena nnanson. Na saa na yɛduu Roma' (Acts 28:13-14).
Christians from Rome come out to meet hi: Kristofo a wofi Roma ba bɛhyia no wɔ Apio Gua ne Ahɔhodan Abiɛsa (Acts 28:15).
Where tradition says Paul's ship ran agr: Baabi a amammerɛ ka sɛ Paulo hyɛn kɔsɛnee wɔ Malta.
The ship strikes a sandbar and all reach: Hyɛn no kɔbɔ anwea tataw bi ho na wɔn nyinaa du asase so dwoodwoo (Acts 27:39-44).
A viper fastens on Paul's hand as he gat: Ɔwɔ bi bɔ Paulo nsa mu bere a ɔreboaboa nnyansin ano, na ɔpopa gu a ɛnyɛ no hwee (Acts 28:3-6).
Paul heals the father of Publius, the is: Paulo sa Publio, supɔw no panyin, agya yare (Acts 28:7-10).
A statue of St Paul stands on St Paul's: Ɔhotefo Paulo ohoni si Ɔhotefo Paulo Supɔw so wɔ po kokwaa no mu. Malta de Ogyefuo 10 di Ɔhotefo Paulo Hyɛn Bɔ Afahyɛ.
The Roman capital of Cyprus, where the p: Kipro Roma ahenkurow, baabi a amrado Sergio Paulo gyee di.
Paul and Barnabas preach in the synagogu: Paulo ne Barnaba ka asɛm wɔ Salamis hyiadan mu (Acts 13:5).
At Paphos the magician Elymas is struck: Pafo wɔbɔ ɔkɔmfo Elimas anifura, na amrado Sergio Paulo gye di (Acts 13:6-12). Efi ha no Luka frɛ Saulo 'Paulo'.
St Paul's Pillar at the church of Agia K: Wɔkyerɛ Ɔhotefo Paulo Dua a ɛwɔ Agia Kyriaki Chrysopolitissa asɔredan ho sɛ baabi a wɔbɔɔ Paulo mmaa. Katolekfo ne Anglikanfo de asɔredan no di dwuma.
Greek city of Libya, home of Simon who c: Libia Greek kurow, Simon a ɔsoaa Yesu asɛndua no ne Yason a n'abakɔsɛm bɛyɛɛ 2 Makabeofo no kurom.
Simon, a Cyrenian, 'the father of Alexan: Simon, Kireneni, 'Aleksander ne Rufo agya', wɔhyɛ no ma ɔsoa asɛndua no (Mark 15:21).
2 Maccabees condenses the five books of: 2 Makabeofo bɔ Yason a ofi Kirene nhoma anum no mu tiawa (2 Maccabees 2:19-32).
Men of Cyrene first preach the Lord Jesu: Kirene mmarima na wodii kan kaa Awurade Yesu ho asɛm kyerɛɛ Greekfo wɔ Antiokia (Acts 11:20).
Royal city of Nubia, whose queens bore t: Nubia ahenkurow, a n'ahemmaa kuraa abodin Kandake, te sɛ ɔhemmaa a ɔpanyin a Filipo bɔɔ no asu no som no.
Tirhakah, king of Cush, marches against: Tirhaka, Kus hene, ko tia Sanherib (2 Kings 19:9).
'Look, there is water. What is to preven: 'Hwɛ, nsuo ni. Dɛn na ɛbɛsiw me kwan sɛ wɔbɛbɔ me asu?' Kandake ahemfie ɔpanyin no gye asubɔ na ɔde anigye kɔ ne kwan (Acts 8:26-39).
The Ethiopian official is honoured as on: Wɔde nidi ma Ethiopiani ɔpanyin no sɛ Amanamanfo a wodii kan gyee asubɔ no mu baako, ansa na Kornelio reba.
